sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! Python Village is full of signs, conversations and letters. In games, characters talk and names shine on the screen. Today we play with text, which we call strings. Want to print a word backwards?
A string is a sequence of characters inside quotes. You join strings with plus, repeat them with a star, and measure how many characters they have with len. Spaces and apostrophes count too!

ekran.kod:
first = "Pi"
second = "ko"
print(first + second)
print("ha" * 3)
print(len("Piko's Adventure"))

sahneler.anlatim: Every letter has a position number, and counting starts at zero. Minus one gives the last letter. A slice from zero to three doesn't include three. And with a step of minus one, the word flips backwards!

Strings come with their own tools, called methods. strip removes spaces at the edges, upper makes everything uppercase, title capitalizes each word, count counts, and replace swaps one piece of text for another.

ekran.kod:
name = "  piko  "
print(name.strip().upper())
print("python village".title())
print("banana".count("a"))
print("hello world".replace("world", "Piko"))

sahneler.anlatim: My favorite tool: the f-string! Put an f before the quotes, and variables inside curly braces are replaced by their values. You can even call a method inside the braces.

ekran.kod:
name = "Piko"
gold = 42
print(f"{name} carries {gold} gold coins.")
print(f"{name.upper()} is coming!")
ekran.cikti:
Piko carries 42 gold coins.
PIKO is coming!

sahneler.anlatim: Try to join text and a number with plus, and Python gives you a TypeError again: you can only add text to text. Your rescuers are ready: an f-string or the str function.

ekran.cikti: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str

sahneler.anlatim: A hint: in asks whether one piece of text is inside another. Now tell me: what does this code print?
The slice from one to four: y, t, h. Four isn't included! And yes, t h appears in the word, so in says True.

In the tasks you'll write a sign in shouting capital letters, catch the first and last letter of a name, and build a level message with an f-string. In the challenge you'll hunt words that read the same backwards, like level!
